artifacts.name: FCOA Canonical Memory & Intelligence Fabric Node

capability_deltas: FCOA-Ω now distinguishes device activity, route reachability and GUI-control qualification as separate states; one connector failure can never by itself produce a DEVICE_OFFLINE or capability-absent claim.

User-visible or screenshot-observed Windows activity is recorded as OBSERVED_ACTIVE evidence, while control reachability is independently tested across direct GUI/computer-use, remote terminal, local device helper, LocalLLM bridge, VM/browser and other qualified routes.

When a terminal route is reachable but no GUI action is exposed, FCOA automatically bootstraps the FCOA Device-Control helper or Win32 SendInput/screen-capture mechanism instead of declaring GUI control unavailable.

If no route is currently reachable, FCOA must classify ACTIVE_BUT_NOT_CURRENTLY_REACHABLE or UNKNOWN_NOT_ABSENT as appropriate, complete an estate census, and harvest/bind a changed mechanism before making an absence claim.
The registered Remote Desktop Commander state is route-specific evidence only; it must not override contradictory fresh evidence from other surfaces.

llm_context.external_effect_rule: Keyboard/mouse reachability does not enlarge provider/external authority.

route_deltas: Before any device-offline or GUI-capability-absent conclusion, run the multi-surface census and preserve route-scoped evidence separately.
A failed direct ping marks only that route UNREACHABLE; if Windows is user/screenshot-observed active, state becomes OBSERVED_ACTIVE_BUT_CONTROL_ROUTE_UNREACHABLE rather than DEVICE_OFFLINE.
If any terminal/process route is reachable, automatically bootstrap the FCOA Device-Control helper or a bounded Win32 input bridge and verify with screen/cursor/foreground readback.
If a direct computer-use/GUI connector becomes available, qualify it independently and prefer it ahead of terminal fallbacks.

If no current control route is reachable, build/bind an outbound device bridge rather than asking the owner to repeat routine troubleshooting; owner action is requested only when no safe machine path exists.
Never claim full keyboard/mouse access from source/build proof alone; require live authorized route readback.
summary: Correct FCOA device-reachability logic so connector-specific failure can never be mistaken for Windows/device absence; add multi-surface census and automatic GUI-control fallback/harvest routing.
warnings: The supplied screenshot proves Windows 11 is visibly active, but does not by itself prove that this chat can inject input into that session.
Remote Desktop Commander currently reports no connected device available to this chat; that is now classified as a route-specific outage, not a device-offline fact.
Live full keyboard/mouse control remains unproven until one authorized control route is reachable and passes benign input/readback verification.
